correctness.rationale: At atomic round 0 the ordered-pair colors of C_n distinguish distances 0,1 and collect >=2 as one class. In round r, all d<=2^r are individually separated while all d>2^r are one far class; exact-exact intermediate-pair witnesses distinguish fresh distances up to 2^(r+1), and for d>2^(r+1) only exact-far, far-exact and far-far counts occur with constant multiplicities by cycle distance symmetry. A far class of cardinality one means stable, yielding r=min{r:floor(n/2)<=2^r+1}; 0 for 3<=n<=5. The C^2 lower bound n>=6 follows because C_n and C_3 disjoint union C_(n-3) have equal order and constant one-dimensional color refinement; C^3 expresses fixed-size connectivity by recursively reusing three variables, and degree 2 and cardinality specify C_n. Independently implemented entire tuple-level refinement for n=3..18, totaling 47 rounds, including distance partitions; all match the formula.

value.rationale: Cycles are the most natural connected 2-regular graphs, on which one-dimensional refinement cannot extract vertex information. The exact two-dimensional stabilization complexity benchmarks propagation of geodesic distances within the important circulant class and relates round complexity to the first finite-order failure of two-variable graph identification. It is an all-n structural formula, not an arbitrary tiny case.

scientific_limitations: Only finite undirected simple cycles and standard atomic pair initial colors; not a uniform single first-order definition of all cycles.
Finite direct tests end at n=18 independently (source script checks farther); the all-n result follows from the induction, not experimental extrapolation.
